extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: Visual Genome is a dataset connecting language and vision using crowdsourced dense image annotations. It contains over 108,249 images, each annotated with an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships between objects. The dataset includes region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases are canonicalized to WordNet synsets. The dataset contains over 4 million objects, 1.6 million attributes, 1.8 million relationships, and 1.7 million question-answer pairs.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bernstein, M. S., & Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) were launched on AMT, where each HIT involved creating descriptions, questions and answers, or region graphs. Each HIT was designed such that workers earn anywhere between $6-$8 per hour. Over 33,000 unique workers contributed to the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Visual Genome dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These images are real-world, non-iconic images that were uploaded onto Flickr by users. The images range from as small as 72 pixels wide to as large as 1280 pixels wide, with an average width of 500 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 6 months of data collection after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question-answer pairs are canonicalized to WordNet synsets. Stanford NLP tools are used to extract noun phrases, which are then mapped to their most frequent matching synset in WordNet according to WordNet lexeme counts. Hand-crafted mapping rules are applied for common failure cases (30 rules for objects, 15 for attributes, 20 for relationships). Attributes are normalized based on morphology (stemming). For relationships, prepositions are excluded and verb synsets are matched to WordNet sentence frames. Scene graphs are constructed by merging region graphs, combining objects with bounding box overlap over union of 0.8.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Region descriptions are preprocessed by removing all non-alphanumeric characters, lowercasing, and stripping excess whitespace. For attribute and relationship experiments, all instances are lowercased, lemmatized, and stripped of excess whitespace. BLEU score thresholds (set to 0.7) are used to ensure diversity in region descriptions. Bounding boxes must satisfy coverage and quality requirements. Stanford's dependency parser is used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions for object extraction. Objects from different region graphs are merged if their bounding boxes have an overlap over union of 0.8.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were collected through a multi-stage crowdsourcing pipeline on Amazon Mechanical Turk. For region descriptions: workers draw bounding boxes and write descriptions, with subsequent workers encouraged to write descriptions not previously written, enforced using BLEU score thresholds. For objects: workers extract objects from descriptions and draw bounding boxes satisfying coverage and quality requirements. For attributes and relationships: workers add attributes to objects and connect pairs of objects with relationships based on region description text. For scene graphs: workers confirm co-referenced objects across region graphs. For QA pairs: workers write freeform and region-based question-answer pairs following rules about question types and avoiding ambiguity. All annotations go through a verification stage using majority voting (3 workers per annotation, at least 2 must agree) or rapid judgments for objects.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification is conducted using two strategies: majority voting and rapid judgments. Majority voting involves three unique workers looking at each annotation and voting on whether it is factually correct; an annotation is added if at least two out of three workers verify it is correct. Rapid judgments are used to speed up verification of objects. Canonicalization precision and recall are evaluated on held-out test sets: Objects achieved 88.0% precision and 98.5% recall; Attributes achieved 85.7% precision and 95.9% recall; Relationships achieved 92.9% precision and 88.5% recall. Visual Genome HITs achieved a 94.1% retention rate.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to enable cognitive computer vision tasks such as image description, question answering, and robotic interactions. It is intended to advance image search, question answering, and robotic interactions by enabling models to understand interactions and relationships between objects in images.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as the top synsets include humans playing sports. There is also a bias towards certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) due to the image source. 93.02% of crowd workers contributed from the United States, which may introduce cultural and linguistic biases in annotations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. The dataset's region descriptions have an average of only 5 words. Current models trained on the dataset are unable to reason about complex images, as demonstrated by low accuracy in region description generation experiments. The QA answers exhibit a long-tail distribution, with the top 1000 frequent answers covering only 64.1% of correct answers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for: attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, semantic image retrieval, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, and scene graph generation. The dataset is designed as a general-purpose representation of the visual world without bias toward a particular task.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs. Each annotation is verified by 3 workers (majority voting).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Geographic distribution: United States 93.02%, Philippines 1.29%, Kenya 1.13%, India 0.94%, Russia 0.50%, Canada 0.47%, Others 2.65%. Age range: 18 to 68 years old, with majority between 25 and 34 years old. Gender: 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions for object extraction. Stanford NLP tools used to extract noun phrases for canonicalization. word2vec used for semantic analysis of descriptions. BLEU score used programmatically to enforce diversity in region descriptions.
